module_summary: cuesupport.cpp is the Ember (PS1 .cue core) backend: EMBER/games folder scan, discs.txt manifest, launch-argument validation, Ember settings.txt rewrite, rename, size, RetroGEM barcode, and the union of POPSTARTER and Ember rows into one PS1 list (ps1FillGameList, ps1DropTwins). discsupport.cpp (RA overlay builds only) hashes a physical disc on the IO worker and launches it in RetroAchievements disc mode. ethsupport.cpp is the SMB1/SMB2/NFS network game source: driver selection and loading, logon/share open, reconnect/refresh on the IO worker, the EthSource GameSource (list, launch on OPL core or Neutrino, VCD/Ember launches, VMC setup), on top of netsupport's TCP/IP stack. ethsupport.h and favsupport.h declare the EthSupport and FavSupport singleton classes plus the free-function C-style API that forwards to them.

reusable_helpers.name: cueSep
reusable_helpers.what: path separator for a device prefix: backslash when the prefix ends in one (SMB), else slash

reusable_helpers.name: cueWriteAll
reusable_helpers.what: write() loop until the whole buffer is written or a short write fails

reusable_helpers.name: cueRewriteSettings
reusable_helpers.what: rewrites a key:value text file in memory, replacing or removing managed keys and keeping all other lines

reusable_helpers.name: cueLineSetsKey
reusable_helpers.what: case-insensitive test whether a config line sets a given key (skips blanks, # and ; comments)

reusable_helpers.name: cueNameLaunchable
reusable_helpers.what: validates a folder/file name for Ember (no .., separators, colon, length cap)

reusable_helpers.name: saveIconPs1Directory
reusable_helpers.what: builds a PS1 game's own folder path for POPSTARTER or Ember (VMC location)

reusable_helpers.name: ps1TwinKey
reusable_helpers.what: strips POPSTARTER XX./SB./EL./SM. prefixes and a leading disc ID to get a comparable title key

reusable_helpers.name: ps1DropTwins
reusable_helpers.what: removes duplicate titles between two concatenated row sets, packing a parallel array along

reusable_helpers.name: discSupportPrefix
reusable_helpers.what: settings home path with a trailing separator, failing on truncation

reusable_helpers.name: ethReadOnlyCfgDir
reusable_helpers.what: CFG folder beside the settings home for read-only devices, created once per folder

reusable_helpers.name: smbOpenShare
reusable_helpers.what: async SMB2 OPENSHARE with CONNECTSTATE polling, falling back to the blocking devctl

findings.title: One-line free forwarders duplicate EthSupport/FavSupport methods and netsupport (21 wrappers)
findings.problem: Every public EthSupport/FavSupport operation exists twice: as a class method and as a free function whose whole body is `return gXxxSupport.method(...)` (eth: ethIsNfs, ethShareChosen, ethIsSMBShareConnected, ethEnsureSMBShareConnected, ethRequestCheckedRefresh, ethRequestReconnect, ethResolveIsoFavourite; fav: favGetItemSourceMode, favGetFlags, favGetItemKind, favGetArtMode, favRemoveByIndex, addFavouriteItem, removeFavouriteByIdAndText, favGetItemDisplay, favGetItemStarred, favToggleByIndex). Four more eth functions only forward to netsupport (ethApplyConfig, ethGetModulesLoaded, ethGetNetConfig, ethGetDHCPStatus). gEthSupport/gFavSupport are already extern in the same headers.
findings.fix: Pick one API. Simplest: callers use gEthSupport.x()/gFavSupport.x() (and netApplyConfig/netGetModulesLoaded/netGetConfig/netGetDHCPStatus) directly; delete the 21 forwarders and their prototypes, moving the useful prototype comments onto the methods. Update the source-text tests that stub or scrape these names.
findings.benefit: ~21 forwarders x 4 lines + ~40 prototype/comment lines in the two headers = ~110 lines removed, ~50 call sites renamed (INFERRED from cited ranges). ELF effect small: forwarders are non-static, no section GC assumed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read every forwarder body at the cited lines; grep -rn 'return gFavSupport\.' favsupport.cpp shows the 10 fav forwarders; grep of the eth names over src: callers in ui/guisettings.cpp, guigame.cpp, guifilemgr.cpp, menuitems.cpp, sources/vcdsupport.cpp, supportbase.cpp, achievements.cpp, ranet.cpp, nettime.cpp, lwnbdctl.cpp, platform/system.cpp, debug.cpp, udpfssupport.cpp, bdmsupport.cpp, appsupport.cpp. ethApplyConfig only caller: src/platform/debug.cpp:72 (debug overlay); ethGetDHCPStatus only caller: ranet.cpp:816 (RA). 21 .github/scripts/*.py files mention some of these names (stubs/scrapes) and must be updated.

findings.title: Ember launch preflight copied in four launchCue legs (ETH, BDM, MMCE, UDPFS) plus an HDD variant
findings.problem: Each leg repeats the same sequence with the same messages: cueNameLaunchable -> _STR_EMBER_BAD_NAME, cueResolveEmber -> _STR_EMBER_NOT_FOUND, cueResolveEmberBios -> _STR_EMBER_BIOS_MISSING, cuePrepareLaunch, cueApplySettings, cueGameHasImage -> _STR_EMBER_NO_DISC, then cuePrepareRetroGemBarcode. Only the prefix and (for MMCE/BDM-SDC) an SIO2 quiesce differ; HDD has its own error cleanup.
findings.fix: Add one cuesupport function (e.g. cueLaunchPreflight(prefix, name, configSet, emberElf, launchName)) that performs the check sequence with its messages and returns 1/0; call it from the ETH, BDM, MMCE and UDPFS legs, keeping their device-specific steps around it. Leave HDD as is or have it call the helper and do its restore on 0. Update test_ember_disc_selection.py:186-204, which asserts the order inside each leg.
findings.justification: The same ~18-line sequence is written four times; one ~22-line helper replaces ~70 lines, and a future change to the launch checks (as the BIOS check and image probe were added) happens once instead of five times.
findings.benefit: ~4 x 18 lines replaced by 4 calls + ~22-line helper = ~45 lines net (INFERRED from cited ranges).
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:1050-1096, bdmlaunch.cpp:60-118, mmcesupport.cpp:1195-1240, udpfssupport.cpp:830-867, hddsupport.cpp:2190-2231. grep cueResolveEmberBios( over src: exactly these five legs. .github/scripts/test_ember_disc_selection.py:188-204 lists the five legs and checks call order per body.

findings.title: CueSupport and DiscSupport are wrapper classes around free functions; DiscSupport::launch is declared but never defined
findings.problem: CueSupport is stateless with one method, gameHasImage, reached only through the cueGameHasImage forwarder; gCueSupport has no other use. DiscSupport holds one volatile int, its methods are reached only through discCheckBusy/discCheckSupportDeferred and a discCheckWorker trampoline, and it declares launch() (line 34) which has no definition and no caller (discLaunch is a free function).
findings.fix: Put the gameHasImage body into cueGameHasImage and delete CueSupport, gCueSupport and the header comment/class. In discsupport.cpp replace the class with a file-static `volatile int discBusy` and plain functions (discCheckBusy, discCheckSupportDeferred, static discCheckWorker), deleting the forwarders and the undefined launch() declaration.
findings.benefit: ~22 lines in cuesupport + ~20 in discsupport removed (INFERRED from cited ranges); no measurable ELF change.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'CueSupport|gCueSupport|gameHasImage' over the repo: only cuesupport.cpp:35,912,958, cuesupport.h:227-235 and a docs plan line; callers use cueGameHasImage (ethsupport, bdmlaunch, mmce, hdd, udpfs). grep 'DiscSupport|gDiscSupport|discCheckWorker' : only discsupport.cpp and docs; no 'DiscSupport::launch' definition anywhere. test_ra_disc.py:220-234 calls the free functions discCheckBusy/discCheckSupportDeferred/discCheckWorker/discLaunch, which the fix keeps. discsupport.cpp is compiled only by the RA overlay (brief section 3).

findings.title: Remember-last-played save block copied 9 times across sources
findings.problem: The identical 4-line block `if (gRememberLastPlayed) { configSetStr(configGetByType(CONFIG_LAST), "last_played", startup); host::app().saveConfig(CONFIG_LAST, 0); }` appears nine times; only the startup expression differs (game->startup or startup).
findings.fix: Add one supportbase function sbRememberLastPlayed(const char *startup) holding the block and call it from the nine launch paths.
findings.justification: Nine copies of the same 4 lines; a 6-line helper replaces 36 lines with 9 calls, net ~21 lines, and the CONFIG_LAST key/save policy lives in one place.
findings.benefit: 36 lines -> 9 calls + 6-line helper = ~21 lines net (INFERRED from cited ranges).
findings.evidence: grep '"last_played", game->startup' over src: ethsupport x2, bdmlaunch x2, hddsupport x2, mmcesupport x1, udpfssupport x1; httpsupport.cpp:799-802 same block with `startup`. Read each with context. Other gRememberLastPlayed uses (opl.cpp:732, gui.cpp:240, menusys.cpp:2855) are reads, not this block.

findings.title: PS2-logo probe (open, CheckPS2Logo, close) copied 5 times in ETH, MMCE and UDPFS launch paths
findings.problem: Each copy is `if (gPS2Logo) { fd = open(path, O_RDONLY, 0666); if (fd >= 0) { EnablePS2Logo = CheckPS2Logo(fd, 0); close(fd); } }`, identical except for the path variable.
findings.fix: Add one helper next to CheckPS2Logo in src/platform/util.cpp (e.g. CheckPS2LogoPath(const char *path), returning 0 when gPS2Logo is off or the open fails) and replace the five blocks with one-line calls.
findings.justification: Five identical 6-7 line blocks; an ~9-line helper replaces ~33 lines with five calls, net ~19 lines.
findings.benefit: ~33 lines -> 5 calls + ~9-line helper = ~19 lines net (INFERRED from cited ranges).
findings.evidence: grep 'EnablePS2Logo = CheckPS2Logo(fd, 0)' over src: ethsupport x2, mmcesupport x1, udpfssupport x2 in this exact shape; bdmlaunch.cpp:846-847 reads it inside a part loop and hddsupport.cpp:2790 uses an LBA, so those stay. CheckPS2Logo defined at src/platform/util.cpp:784.

findings.title: Repeated list-reset, list-free and guard blocks in ethsupport.cpp; update() re-implements count()
findings.problem: The scan-state reset (ulSizePrev=-2, mtimes, counts, retry flags) is written three times; cleanUp and shutdown free and zero both lists with the same 6 lines; checkedRefreshSmb repeats its 5-line ownership guard; the last 5 lines of update() are the body of count(); and launch() re-tests game != NULL at 1298 after returning on NULL at 1291.
findings.fix: Give EthSupport one resetScan() and one freeLists() method and use them at the cited places; make the guard a local lambda or bool helper; end update() with `return count(itemList);`; drop the redundant game != NULL test.
findings.justification: Two small methods replace five copies of 5-8 lines each; net reduction about 20 lines and the reset fields cannot drift apart between init, reconnect and share selection.
findings.benefit: ~20 lines net (INFERRED: 3 reset copies ~20 lines, 2 free copies 12 lines, guard 5, count tail 5, minus ~16 lines of helpers).
findings.evidence: Read all cited ranges in ethsupport.cpp; the reset copies differ only in which fields they include (init also NULLs the list pointers, reconnect keeps them per its comment at 603-605), so resetScan needs a flag or the NULLing stays at init.

findings.title: ethReadOnlyCfgDir duplicates the read-only CFG folder block in BdmSource::config
findings.problem: Both build `<home>[/]CFG/`, keep a static madeCfgDir[256] and mkdir the folder once per path, with the same comments; ~14 lines are the same. They differ only in the 'home is on this read-only device' test (nfs: prefix vs bdmIsReadOnlyPath) and ETH also accepting EEXIST.
findings.fix: Move one sbReadOnlyCfgDir(cfgDir, size, excludeHome) into supportbase.cpp (taking the home-exclusion result as a parameter, and accepting EEXIST for both) and call it from both sources.
findings.justification: Removes one of two near-identical copies (~14 lines net) and one of two 256-byte static madeCfgDir buffers; the EEXIST difference means BDM currently retries mkdir on every selection when the folder already exists.
findings.benefit: ~14 lines and 256 bytes .bss removed (INFERRED: one static char madeCfgDir[256] dropped).
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.cpp:1526-1556 and bdmsupport.cpp:2045-2073 side by side; grep 'madeCfgDir' finds only these two definitions.

findings.title: POPSTARTER SMB preparation result -> message mapping duplicated in ETH launchVcd and APPS
findings.problem: Both call vcdPreparePopstarterSmbLaunch and then map its five vcd_popsnet_ensure_t results to the same five msgBox strings with the same returns (20 identical lines).
findings.fix: Do the mapping once: let vcdsupport show the message (e.g. a vcdPreparePopstarterSmbLaunchUi wrapper returning 1 only for READY) and have both callers return on 0.
findings.justification: Two identical 20-line blocks; one ~16-line function replaces both, net ~20 lines, and a new result code cannot be handled in one caller and missed in the other.
findings.benefit: ~40 lines -> 2 calls + ~16-line function = ~20 lines net (INFERRED from cited ranges).
findings.evidence: grep 'VCD_POPSNET_INVALID|_STR_POPSTARTER_SMB_NEEDS_STATIC' over src: only ethsupport.cpp:1022,1029, appsupport.cpp:1156,1163 and the producer in vcdsupport.cpp; read both blocks.

findings.title: Small duplicates inside cuesupport.cpp: settings value tables twice, extension loop twice, nine free() pairs
findings.problem: cueSaveGameSettings and cueApplySettings each declare the same four static value tables (timing, dither, shading, controller); cueResolveGameImage re-implements cueNameIsDiscImage's extension loop instead of reusing it with an index result; cueRewriteSettingsFile frees before/after on each of nine exits (18 lines).
findings.fix: Move the value tables to file scope once; make cueNameIsDiscImage return the matched extension index (or -1) and use it in cueResolveGameImage; in cueRewriteSettingsFile use one allocation of two halves or one cleanup label so the buffers are freed in one place.
findings.benefit: ~22 lines removed (INFERRED: 4 table lines, ~6 loop lines, ~12 free lines); duplicate tables are already merged by the compiler only if identical-data folding applies, so possibly ~60 bytes .rodata (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read the cited ranges. test_ember_settings.py extracts cueRewriteSettings/cueLineSetsKey/cueWantSetting by signature (header comment cuesupport.h:223-226); tables moved to file scope must be added to that harness if it extracts cueApplySettings.

findings.title: Prefix separator rule re-implemented six times (cueSep, vcdSep and four inline copies)
findings.problem: 'backslash if the prefix ends with one, else slash' is written as cueSep, as vcdSep (identical body) and inline in saveIconPs1Directory (which could call cueSep in the same file), EthSource::launchVcd, favsupport and supportbase. The cueSep comment says it is kept local on purpose, but the two bodies are byte-identical.
findings.fix: Declare one static inline helper in supportbase.h (e.g. sbPrefixSep) and use it in all six places; delete cueSep and vcdSep (or make them aliases while the source-text tests that extract `static char cueSep(` are updated).
findings.benefit: ~12 lines removed (INFERRED from cited ranges); no ELF change worth stating.
findings.evidence: grep "== '\\\\') ? '\\\\' : '/'" over src: cuesupport.cpp:44, vcdsupport.cpp:776, ethsupport.cpp:1036, favsupport.cpp:1270, supportbase.cpp:1355; cuesupport.cpp:127 same rule without parentheses. Tests test_ember_fatfs_images.py:30, test_ember_disc_selection.py:32, test_retrogem_ember.py:27 extract 'static char cueSep(' by signature.

findings.title: EthSupport exposes its private fields through 12 reference accessors
findings.problem: prefix(), base(), setBase(), ulSizePrev(), modifiedCDPrev(), modifiedDVDPrev(), gameCount(), games(), ps1GameCount(), ps1Games(), ps1ScanFailed(), ps1ScanRetries() return mutable references (or raw pointers) to private members, and EthSource assigns through them (e.g. ethsupport.cpp:729-735, 815-818). The fields are public in all but syntax.
findings.fix: Make those members public (drop the trailing underscore or keep it) and delete the 12 accessors, or make EthSource a friend; either removes a layer that encapsulates nothing.
findings.benefit: ~14 header lines removed (INFERRED); call sites change from gameCount() to gameCount_.
findings.evidence: Read ethsupport.h:63-139 and every EthSource method in ethsupport.cpp:716-1671; all accessor uses are reads or assignments through the returned reference.

findings.title: cueEmberFolder() is a speculative accessor returning a constant
findings.problem: cueEmberFolder only returns EMBER_FOLDER_DEFAULT; its comment says a configurable folder 'can arrive later as a setting'. No such setting exists; the header tells callers to use the accessor, never the macro.
findings.fix: Delete cueEmberFolder and use EMBER_FOLDER_DEFAULT (or rename it EMBER_FOLDER) at its five uses; update the five test scripts that extract or stub the accessor.
findings.benefit: ~8 lines removed (INFERRED); no ELF change (static, inlined).
findings.evidence: grep 'EMBER_FOLDER_DEFAULT|cueEmberFolder' over the repo: definition cuesupport.cpp:47-53, uses at 63, 91, 133, 824, 855; macro cuesupport.h:113; tests test_ember_scan_missing_core.py:71, test_ember_fatfs_images.py:30, test_ember_disc_selection.py:32, test_ember_settings.py:515, test_ps1_save_icons.py:22, test_retrogem_ember.py:27, test_info_size_ps1.py:55. No config key for an Ember folder name.

findings.title: Defensive argument checks in cuesupport static settings helpers that their only caller already rules out
findings.problem: cueRewriteSettings re-validates NULL pointers, negative sizes and wantCount==0 although its only caller (cueRewriteSettingsFile:695-730) has already rejected wantCount<=0 and passes two fresh buffers; the wantCount==0 copy branch is reached only by test_ember_settings.py:415. cueWantSetting checks list/count/key/values for NULL though all nine calls pass locals and string literals.
findings.fix: Delete the wantCount==0 branch and the NULL checks (keep the setting range check in cueWantSetting); adjust the one harness case that passes wantCount 0, or keep it since the loop would still copy an LF-only input unchanged.
findings.evidence: grep 'cueRewriteSettings(' over the repo: definition 575, call 730, harness calls test_ember_settings.py:389,416 (the wantCount-0 case is line 415 via expect()). grep 'cueWantSetting(' : nine calls at 813-819 and 848-852, all with local arrays and literals.

findings.title: Thirteen SMB2-only diagLog breadcrumbs wrapped around SMB init steps
findings.problem: Every SMB2 init step is bracketed by `if (gSMBDialect == SMB_DIALECT_V2) diagLog("SMB2 init: X enter")` and a matching 'returned %d' line, in every build (diagLog is always compiled, include/diaglog.h:13). The enter/return pairs look like leftover bring-up tracing for the smb2man work; the outcome already ends in gNetworkStartup and the LOG lines.
findings.fix: Keep the two smb2LogIopFree calls and one line with the final LOGON/ECHO/OPENSHARE result; delete the per-step enter/return pairs and their gSMBDialect guards.
findings.benefit: ~20 lines and roughly 400 bytes of .rodata format strings removed (INFERRED: ~10 strings of ~40 bytes).
findings.evidence: Read all cited lines; diaglog.h:4-13 and src/platform/diaglog.cpp:14-31 show diagLog writes a 16 KB RAM ring saved by Drive Status > Save Diagnostics in all builds. INFERRED: that the per-step pairs are no longer needed for support; the owner may want to keep some.

findings.title: Stale comments in ethsupport.h, favsupport.h and ethsupport.cpp
findings.problem: ethDeinitModules is called 'otherwise unused' but is called from lwnbdctl.cpp:86 and EthSource::cleanUp/shutdown; favsupport.h names favsupport.c/opl.c/gui.c (now .cpp) and documents an isVcd parameter that is now `kind`; EthSource::image says texDiscoverLoad 'above' already tried, but the call is texDiscoverArt and keeps a needless temporary; cuesupport.cpp cites vcdsupport.c.
findings.fix: Correct or delete these comments; return texDiscoverArt(...) directly in EthSource::image.
findings.evidence: grep ethDeinitModules over src: lwnbdctl.cpp:86, ethsupport.cpp:1602,1623; favsupport.h:165-166 prototypes take `int kind`; ethsupport.cpp:1566 calls texDiscoverArt.
